title: Warm up with the Python this course uses
brief: Write ten small functions and one tiny class: ints, strings, lists, dicts, hex, bytes, and a function that returns assembly text.
hints: Each function is short. If the body is longer than four lines, look for a simpler way.
An f-string puts values into text: `f"Hello, {name}!"` replaces `{name}` with the value of `name`.
`int("ff", 16)` reads a hex string, and `hex(255)` gives `'0xff'`. `bin(5)` gives `'0b101'`, and `"101".zfill(8)` pads with zeros on the left.
`"Hi".encode("ascii")` gives `b'Hi'`. Indexing or looping over a `bytes` value gives ints from 0 to 255. `f"{x:02x}"` formats an int as two lowercase hex digits.
For `word_counts`, loop over `text.lower().split()` and use `counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1`.
A triple-quoted f-string can span lines. Put `.globl {name}` on one line, `{name}:` on the next, then the two instructions, indented by four spaces.
